payload.rebuttal: fixed: Every witness in the diff built its worktree under git's sha1 default, so the dynamic `fmt=$($worktree_prefix rev-parse --show-object-format)` line and a hardcoded `fmt="sha1"` produced identical results in every test: `GIT_DEFAULT_HASH=sha256` in criterion 3's test only affects a naive fresh `git init`'s own default, never the pre-existing worktree's real format, which stayed sha1 throughout. I confirmed this by hand-mutating the source to `fmt="sha1"` and running the full suite: 47 of 48 tests stayed green, proving the line had no witness. I added `test_export_patch_reads_a_worktree_whose_own_object_format_is_sha256` in tests/test_worktree.py, which builds a worktree with `git init --object-format=sha256` directly, proves that format is real via `rev-parse --show-object-format` before calling `export_patch`, and asserts the patch comes back correctly. Under the same hand-applied `fmt="sha1"` mutant, this new test is the only one that fails, with `export_patch` raising `CellRuntimeError` because the fresh dir's sha1 objects/info/alternates points at a sha256 object store and the diff errors with 'unknown revision'. Committed as fe075c2, 33 lines, tests/test_worktree.py only; saffron/cell/worktree.py is unchanged from the prior commit.
